title: The Joy of the LORD
backstory: The wall is finished — fifty and two days of work, and Jerusalem has a wall around it again (Nehemiah 6:15). But stones alone cannot make God's people strong. So all the people gather as one man into the street before the water gate and ask Ezra the scribe to bring out the book of the law of Moses (Nehemiah 8:1). What they hear will make them weep (Nehemiah 8:9).

passages.synopsis: All the people gathered as one man in the street before the water gate. They asked Ezra the scribe to bring the book of the law of Moses. From morning until midday he read aloud, and the ears of all the people were attentive. When Ezra opened the book, everyone stood up, and when he blessed the LORD, the people answered, Amen, Amen, and worshipped.

The Levites helped the people understand what was read, giving the sense of every part. When the people understood the law, they began to weep. But Nehemiah, Ezra, and the Levites told them not to mourn, because the day was holy to the LORD. They said to go and feast and share with those who had nothing, for the joy of the LORD is your strength. So the people made great mirth, because they had understood the words.

On the second day the leaders came back to Ezra to learn more of the law. They found written there that Israel should live in booths during the feast of the seventh month. So the people went out, gathered branches, and built leafy booths on their roofs and in their courts. Israel had not kept the feast this way since the days of Joshua, and there was very great gladness.

Later, when the wall of Jerusalem was dedicated, the people offered great sacrifices and rejoiced. God had made them rejoice with great joy. The wives and the children rejoiced too, so that the joy of Jerusalem was heard even afar off.

reflection: When the people understood God's word, their tears turned to great joy. Where do you look for strength when you are sad — and how could God's joy become yours?
